summary.summary: Covering report presenting the draft Annual Governance Statement for 2025/26 (the AGS itself is Appendix 1, a separate document). Two points matter for a lender. First, the draft AGS has been published alongside the council's draft 2025/26 Statement of Accounts, with the final versions due by the 31 January 2027 statutory deadline after a further update in October 2026 — the reporting cycle is on its statutory track. Second, the council says no NEW significant governance issues have arisen since the final 2024/25 AGS was approved in February 2026, but the existing ones continue: the draft focuses on updating progress on financial sustainability, improvement and transformation, governance and internal control, leadership capacity, children's services improvement and partnership working. In short, a council still working through a known list of significant issues, with no fresh deterioration disclosed and no figures in this paper.

signals.headline: Draft AGS 2025/26 published alongside the draft 2025/26 Statement of Accounts, in line with statutory requirements; final accountability statements due by the 31 January 2027 backstop after an October 2026 committee update
signals.why: The unaudited 2025/26 balance sheet is now public and the governance disclosures around it are on the statutory timetable rather than slipping.

compliance.notes: High-quality, Arlingclose-advised strategy: strongest areas are the liability benchmark (charted to the end of the debt profile with all balances and assumptions), the full prudential-indicator suite, the capital strategy/MRP and a comprehensive investment strategy covering the council's ~£60m of service/commercial investments. Weakest areas are formal governance artefacts not restated in the annual documents (no explicit adoption of the TM Code's four clauses; no audit-qualification flag; no explicit sterling-only borrowing statement or paras 51-53 compliance statement; no formal IMPs), and, for a commercial investor, no quantified commercial/service-income dependence ratio. Note: the packet's capital_strategy.url (s134122) was a 2027/28 MTFS-assumptions Cabinet paper with no capital-strategy content; the real Capital/Investment strategies and prudential indicators were read from the MTFS 2026-2030 full report (Annexes 5, 6, B, C). The packet TMSS url (s131504) was a cover report; the real TMSS is Annex 7 (s131505).

news_drafts.headline: Cheshire East uses emergency support to balance budget as adult care costs surge
news_drafts.lead: Cheshire East Council has used £24.995m of exceptional financial support—emergency government funding—to balance its 2026/27 budget. The money was needed to address structural demand growth in adult social care, where the council faces annual increases of about £6m in care costs. In the first quarter alone, adult social care demand was already running £5.5m over budget. The council's savings programmes are delivering only about £3m to £4m across all initiatives, leaving a structural annual gap. Council documents describe the current adult social care system as unable to simultaneously meet rising demand, deliver its legal duties and achieve financial sustainability without transformation.

findings.paper_title: Appendix 1 for Adults Social Care Transformation Plan Update Slide-Deck
findings.headline: The Adult Social Care transformation designed to address structural budget pressures remains in pre-design phase, with implementation deferred to 2027.
findings.detail: The council's long-term response to structural demand growth depends on a major ASC service redesign. As of September 2026, this remains in phase one (Current State Assessment). The Adult Social Care Transformation Board was due to receive sign-off on 21 September 2026. Design phase work spans late 2026 through early 2027, covering service models, organisational structure, and decision-making frameworks. Implementation is scheduled to begin in 2027. This timeline means the council will manage structural budget gaps for at least another 12 months before transformation can contribute to closing them.
findings.matters: The council's ability to close structural annual gaps (£2-3m) depends on transformation outcomes. A lender needs to understand timeline risk: delays in design or implementation would extend the period of structural budget pressure.
findings.figures: Current State Assessment sign-off expected 21/09/26; design phase planned through Q4 2026/Q1 2027; implementation scheduled to begin 2027
findings.quote: We are currently in the first phase of the transformation work, to provide a picture of the Service as-is.

findings.paper_title: Appendix 1 for Adults Social Care Transformation Plan Update Slide-Deck
findings.headline: Adult Social Care savings programmes are delivering only 30-50% of MTFS targets five months into the financial year.
findings.detail: Multiple ASC programmes are significantly behind their stated 2026/27 targets. The Shared Lives programme has delivered £200k of cost avoidance against a £490k target (41% achievement). The PRE (Prevent, Reduce, Enable) programme has delivered £1.37m against a £2.83m target (48% achievement). The Care4CE improvement project shows £900k in identified annualised savings against a £2.01m target, but requires £400k investment to realise net savings of £500k. The Commissioned Care Review programme has delivered £705k in savings to date, but 51 of 181 completed reviews remain onboarded into accounting systems, creating a backlog.
findings.matters: MTFS delivery at only 30-50% of target at mid-year raises questions about either planning assumptions or execution capability. Delivery shortfalls could leave the council with unplanned deficits.
findings.figures: £1.37m cost avoided to date against £2.83m target (PRE); £200k estimated in-year cost avoidance against £490k target (Shared Lives); £705k saved to date (Commissioned Care Review); £900k annualised savings identified with £400k investment required for £500k net delivery (Care4CE)
findings.quote: £200k estimated in-year cost avoidance based on progress to date

findings.paper_title: Appendix 1 for Adults Social Care Transformation Plan Update Slide-Deck
findings.headline: Structural demand growth of £6m annually in Adult Social Care is outpacing the council's savings delivery capacity.
findings.detail: Cheshire East faces sustained demand growth in Adult Social Care of around £6m per year for the next five years, accumulating to £30m in additional budget requirement by 2030/31. This follows a 22% budget increase over the preceding three years. Unit costs are rising 6.4% annually per client—above inflation—while client volumes grow only 1.4%. Current savings programmes are delivering approximately £3-4m total across initiatives, leaving a structural annual gap of roughly £2-3m between demand growth and savings delivery.
findings.matters: A lender assessing long-term financial sustainability must understand whether the council can manage structural demand growth in its largest discretionary budget. Persistent gaps between demand and savings indicate accumulating budget pressure.
findings.figures: Annual growth pressures of around £6m forecast over the next five years; £30mn overall budget increase by 2030/31; budget increased 22% from £138mn in 2023/24 to £169mn in 2026/27; average cost per client rising 6.4% annually
findings.quote: Annual growth pressures of around £6m are forecast over the next five years, representing a £30mn overall budget increase by 2030/31.

findings.paper_title: Adults Social Care Transformation Plan Update
findings.headline: Learning Disability programme has identified £705k savings from 181 reviews to date; programme scope expanded significantly with capital investment requirement.
findings.detail: The Learning Disability programme has completed 181 supported living reviews generating £705k savings, with scope expanded from nine largest providers to all commissioned supported-living providers. Care4CE improvements identified £900k of opportunities, delivering net £500k savings in 2026/27 after £400k buy-out investment, contributing to the full programme target of £5.651m.
findings.matters: This programme contributes £5.100m of the £22.45m savings target; the reliance on £400k capital investment to realise savings represents a liquidity requirement within the transformation funding plan.
findings.figures: £705k to date from 181 reviews; £900k identified; net £500k 2026/27 after £400k investment; £5.651m full programme; £0.551m achieved 2025/26
findings.quote: 181 Supported Living reviews have now been completed and of those 130 onboarded to our systems, generating a current estimated saving to date of around £705,000.

findings.paper_title: Adults Social Care Transformation Plan Update
findings.headline: Current Adult Social Care system cannot simultaneously sustain increasing demand, meet statutory duties, and achieve financial sustainability.
findings.detail: The council characterises its current ASC system as 'reactive rather than preventative', 'fragmented rather than integrated', 'capacity constrained rather than optimised', and 'cost escalating rather than sustainable'. It states the system 'is not designed to manage today's level of demand, complexity, or financial pressure' and that 'incremental change will not address structural issues.'
findings.matters: The transformation savings depend on restructuring the entire service model; failure to implement structural change could result in service failure or cost overruns outside planned savings.
findings.figures: None specific to demand volumes stated
findings.quote: the current system cannot simultaneously meet increasing demand, deliver statutory duties, and achieve financial sustainability
